text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Visiting Chinese President Jiang Zemin assured Pakistan his country would continue its cooperation with Islamabad in the peaceful application of nuclear technology.
- The caretaker government plans to file 12 cases of fraud and misuse of discretionary powers against officials of Commerce Ministry and its four corporations.
- A leader of the militant Shi'ite Sipah-i-Mohammad Pakistan group was shot dead by two gunmen in central Punjab city of Multan.
- The United Arab Emirates is expected to provide $350 million to Pakistan to improve its balance of payment position.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The All Pakistan Solvent Extractors association has urged the government to encourage local production of oil seeds rather than reducing duty on import of edible oils.
- The Association of Shippers' Council of Bangladesh, India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka unanimously elected Pakistan as its next chairman.

- Shahid Javed Burki, advisor on finance, will embark on a two-week tour of Tokyo and Washington from December 4 to reactivate Japan's assistance, restore the standby agreement with the International Monetary Fund and initiate discussion on an extended structural adjustment facility.
- Pakistan's liquid forex reserves rose to $722.5 million on Sunday from a low of $550 million a week ago, sources said.
THE NATION
- The North West Frontier Province government has decided to impose tax on agricultural income and increase the irrigation water charges.

- Blood tests of 1.5 million people carried out in Pakistan showed that 1,033 people were HIV-positive while 64 had full-blown AIDS. There are an estimated 50,000 to 60,000 HIV-positive people in Pakistan.
THE MUSLIM
- Pakistan Oilfields Limited has discovered oil at Minwal, 110 km (68 miles) southwest of Islamabad.
THE NEWS
- A Swiss-based company, Trafigura, has approached the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Resources about buying 12,000 tonnes of raw copper worth $34 million from the Saindak copper and gold project.
- The caretaker government has appointed Nasim Mirza as the new chairman of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd.
--Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
